criteria_results.why: Every item r7 scored blocking is gone, and I verified each by quoting the current bytes rather than trusting the summary: __main__.py's "is what refuses a broken transform"; the section headline; module-contract question 1; the "speaks to correctness" sentence; both intensity reasons; the applied comment; the "Every rule below" absolute; the longitude-constant comment; the test module's first line, both bullets, the endpoint-longitude docstring and the TraceError wording; and the round2 assertion, which now pins the scoped "only RUNTIME field that responds". r7's four accepted replacement texts appear verbatim (or with strictly more evidence attached) at every site. The broad re-grep over all of CODE/ minus CODE/work/ found no sentence that claims the deterministic check observes the generator, its acceptance step, or application: the surviving applications/refusals language is either self-limiting ("does not observe", "not a proof that the transform WAS APPLIED", "speaks to the multiplier FUNCTION") or is about a different object (config modes, passivity, mode gating). The residual items I found are recorded as weaknesses, not as C4 failures, because none of them overstates what the deterministic transform check observes: #1 is a comment paraphrase of the intensity field that still says "the ONE check that can see a broken generator" (stale relative to the now-scoped report text it justifies -- the accepted wording is "the only RUNTIME field that responds"); #2 is the 0.01 sd-convention mismatch; #3/#4 are stale comment details inside the test file. C4's substance (the report no longer claims to observe the generator, and the limitation is declared at every point of use) is met, and the criterion's check items hold literally: verified / not_verified / thinning_clause_is_algebraic_identity present, "property" absent, and the three named test files pass.

weaknesses_found: [non-blocking wording, strongest residual] CODE/leo_sim/tests/test_pre_experiment_trust_round2.py:173-174 comment: '# the reason must point at the ONE check that can see a broken generator, / # now that the deterministic transform check is documented as unable to'.
